newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO counts new buy from start of 97.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO counts new buy from start of 97.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV will consolidate the results of its newly-acquired U.S. bank Standard Federal Bancorp from the start of 1997, an ABN AMRO spokesman said on Thursday.
Spokesman Jules Prast said this applied to the profits from the Michigan-based bank as well as the average financing costs on the $1.95 billion acquisition.
"It's correct that the results of Standard Federal will count as from January 1," he told Reuters.
There had been some uncertainty on when the Dutch bank would start including Standard Federal in its accounts.
ABN AMRO announced the acquisition last November and said in May that it had been finalised.
It was financed through existing cash holdings, carrying net financing costs of four percent, and a $750 million preference share issue, paying a net dividend of 6.5 percent.
ABN AMRO said last November it expected an initial annualised return from the investment of nine percent.
